name: Mountaincart-Abfahrt Brixen im Thale
beschreibung:
Overview
Coasting down alpine gravel trails on three chunky low-profile tires with dual disc brakes: Mountaincarting ranks among the most thrilling summer outdoor adventures in the Kitzbühel Alps. Travelers exploring the Brixental valley will encounter an important geographic detail: direct at the Hochbrixen gondola in Brixen im Thale, there is no designated cart track (the mountain focuses on the Filzalmsee lake adventure world and the SunTrail bike trail). Instead, the official premier mountaincart track of the Kitzbühel Alps is situated just twenty minutes away at the Harschbichlbahn in St. Johann in Tirol. Here, a purpose-built gravel track swoops from the middle station through scenic forest switchbacks all the way down to the valley floor.

Route & Requirements
The Harschbichl mountaincart track begins at the middle station of the Harschbichlbahn at 1,190 meters above sea level and finishes at the valley station at 670 meters. Over a distance of 3.8 kilometers, riders tackle 520 vertical meters of descent. The route winds along dedicated gravel tracks featuring banked curves, straight stretches, and rolling terrain through alpine woods and meadows. The carts are non-motorized, rely solely on gravity, and feature dual independent hydraulic disc brakes with an ultra-low center of gravity that prevents tipping over. Descent time ranges from 15 to 25 minutes depending on braking style. Children aged 5 and older can ride tandem on an adult's cart (up to a combined weight of 120 kg). Independent riding is permitted from age 10 with a minimum height of 140 cm, accompanied by an adult. Helmets are mandatory (rental helmets are included free of charge), and sturdy closed-toe shoes are strictly required. Comprehensive safety instruction is provided before departure. Dogs cannot be taken on the carts.

Getting There
The valley station of the Harschbichlbahn is located at Hornweg 21 in 6380 St. Johann in Tirol. From Brixen im Thale, it is accessible in roughly 20 minutes by private vehicle or via regional ÖBB train to St. Johann in Tirol station (followed by a 12-minute walk). Free parking is available directly at the cable car terminal. Free parking and regional bus stops are also located at the Hochbrixen valley terminal (Liftweg 1) in Brixen im Thale.

Tips
Carts cannot be reserved in advance; issuance operates on a first-come, first-served basis at the middle station upon presenting a valid photo ID as deposit. A combination ticket covering the cable car ascent and the cart descent costs around €35 for adults and €28 for children. Because the gravel track can be dusty in sunshine and damp after rain, durable outdoor attire is strongly recommended. Another scenic 2.1-kilometer cart track in the area is located at Alpengasthof Oberweissbach in Waidring.
